item.title: The Biggest Oil Deal or Theft at Gunpoint? U.S. Claims Majority Control of Venezuela's Oil Reserves
item.description:
The U.S. has struck a deal to take majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s oil reserves, nine months after the U.S. military abducted President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores in a raid on Caracas and two months after The New York Times revealed that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has become the de facto viceroy of Venezuela, effectively controlling Venezuela’s finances, the distribution of its natural resources and its government. The new oil deal gives the Department of Defense a 35% stake in a joint U.S.-Venezuelan private company that now holds 100-year leases to 17 oil fields. It also gives the U.S. the right to buy some of the oil produced at cost — a major triumph for the Trump administration as the war on Iran depletes the United States’ strategic oil reserves. Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez claims U.S. investment in Venezuela’s oil industry will jumpstart the country’s floundering economy, but critics, including Venezuelan economist Francisco Rodríguez, say the deal is not only “unfavorable to Venezuela” but also appears to violate the Venezuelan Constitution.

“The whole history around this is extremely shady,” adds Rodríguez, who previously led Venezuela’s Congressional Budget Office and now teaches at the University of Denver. “It’s clear that this is not a deal that any Venezuelan government would have entered into unless this country had been subject to an invasion, and unless its authorities had been held at gunpoint. So, I think we’ve replaced gunboat diplomacy now for gunpoint diplomacy.”

item.title: Taiwan says 'unpredictable' China strengthens air, sea control nearby
item.description: TAIPEI — An increasingly unpredictable Beijing is tightening its grip on the air and sea around Taiwan, Taipei said in an annual review of the Chinese threat that also said China was learning lessons from issues faced by the United States in waging war on Iran. China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, has never renounced the use of force to bring the island under its control, and sends its military into the waters and airspace around Taiwan on an almost daily basis. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future. The United States supplies Taiwan with weapons while maintaining a policy of ambiguity about whether it would fight to defend it. In its annual report on China's military threat, a copy of which was reviewed by Reuters, Taiwan's defence ministry said the regional security situation "continues to escalate," noting a "rising unpredictability" in China's decision-making due to an "unprecedented" purge of senior military officers. item.title: Over 6,000 infected with Ebola in Congo
item.description: DAKAR — The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed the 6,000 mark, government data showed on Monday. The epidemic has become the largest in the central African country's history, surpassing the previous worst outbreak that lasted from 2018 to 2020. It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has no approved vaccines or treatments. The number of people with confirmed infections has risen to 6,041, and 2,911 of them have died, the communication ministry said on X. Response teams are working in six provinces affected by the outbreak, with a particular focus on Ituri, North Kivu and Haut-Uele, it added.

item.title: Why are Korean films struggling to compete in summer blockbuster race?
item.description: Moviegoers flocked to theaters this summer. “Spider-Man: Brand New” had drawn 8.29 million viewers as of Aug. 27, while “The Odyssey” attracted 7.2 million. With “The Odyssey” showing no signs of slowing down, it is highly likely to surpass the 10 million mark. That will make it the first film to draw more than 10 million viewers here during the summer, traditionally considered peak moviegoing season, since August 2018 when “Along With the Gods: The Last 49 Days” attracted 12.27 million viewers after its release. The number of moviegoers surged in July and August as well. As of Aug. 27, 28.42 million people had visited theaters, up 3.38 million from the 25.04 million who did so during the same period last year. In other words, Korean theaters are enjoying a genuinely lively summer for the first time in years. For theaters that have endured a brutal slump since the COVID-19 pandemic, they must feel like bowing down in gratitude to the two Hollywood films driving the box office. item.title: Suspect arrested after Swiss rave shooting kills 1
item.description: GENEVA — A suspect has been arrested after a weekend shooting at a rave in northern Switzerland that left one person dead and five wounded, police said Monday. The 43-year-old Swiss citizen was arrested during the night, police in Aargau canton (state) said in a statement. They said that investigations into a possible motive are ongoing and that at present they believe the shooting was carried out by a lone perpetrator. The shooting took place in the early hours of Sunday in Aarau, the regional capital. Police have said that a 22-year-old woman died of injuries at the scene. Four men and one woman, between 24 and 27 years old, were taken to the hospital with injuries ranging from minor to severe. Swiss police have said that all of the victims are residents of Switzerland. Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni on Sunday evening identified the woman who was killed and two other victims as Italian citizens.

item.title: 9 Koreans rescued from Nepal floods return home
item.description: Nine out of the 10 Koreans who were safely rescued after being initially stranded following massive flooding in Nepal returned home Monday, their company said. Doosan Enerbility said nine of its employees who were rescued from flood-stricken areas in Nepal arrived in Korea around 2 p.m. They underwent health checks immediately upon arrival and then returned home, with none suffering health problems severe enough to require hospitalization. "The nine employees are physically and mentally exhausted after experiencing a sudden disaster and being stranded," the company said. The remaining employee, the site manager, stayed behind to support search and rescue operations, it added. The 10 employees, who were working on the construction of a hydropower plant in Nepal's Rasuwa district, had been stranded in the area following a massive flash flood and mudslide that struck the area Wednesday. Nine of the 10 were transported by a Nepalese military helicopter to a safer area Thursday, while the site manager evacuated the following day. item.title: Seoul, Tokyo deepen AI cooperation through digital administration
item.description: Seoul and Tokyo are moving to turn their growing digital ties into practical projects, with officials from both cities discussing how artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to reshape public administration. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday that it held an online working-level meeting with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s Digital Service Bureau on Friday, following a digital cooperation agreement signed in April. Nineteen officials from the two cities took part in the meeting, sharing policies on AI literacy, public-sector AI applications and efforts to strengthen AI capabilities among civil servants and residents. Seoul presented major projects under its digital policy programs, while Tokyo introduced initiatives led by its digital strategy division and examples of support for AI use in public administration. The officials also identified areas of common interest and discussed projects that could develop into broader policy exchanges and joint initiatives. The meeting marked the first working-level discussion aimed at turning five areas agreed under the April memorandu

item.title: Korea imposes travel ban on parts of Pakistan
item.description: The foreign ministry on Monday imposed a Level 4 travel ban on parts of Pakistan amid a surge in violence linked to coordinated separatist attacks. The ban — the highest of the country's four-tier travel warning system — will take effect at 11 p.m. in the southwestern province of Balochistan, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Parts of the province are also subject to a travel ban imposed by the Pakistani government. Under the law, those who visit or stay in areas under the highest-level travel ban without special permission can be punished. The ministry urged those planning to visit the region to cancel their trips and those residing there to evacuate.

item.title: Police to disclose identity of suspect in murder of Chinese graduate student
item.description: Police said Monday they will disclose the personal details and photo of a Chinese university lecturer accused of murdering a female Chinese graduate student in the southeastern city of Gyeongsan earlier this month. A deliberation committee decided to publish the name, age and mug shot of the suspect, currently known as a 31-year-old surnamed Jeong, on Tuesday, according to the Gyeongbuk Provincial Police Agency. Jeong is accused of killing the 25-year-old student at his home on Aug. 20, mutilating her body and abandoning the parts in multiple places, including the southeastern city of Gyeongju and Gunpo, south of Seoul. In deciding on the disclosure, the committee considered factors, such as the brutality of the crime, the gravity of the harm and future crime prevention. Jeong's personal details will be published on the Gyeongbuk police agency's website for 30 days until Sept. 30. He was placed under formal arrest Thursday. He has also been charged with obstructing the police's investigation by filing a false missing report after killing the victim and turning off her cellphone near a tra

item.title: Prosecutors seek death penalty for Gwangju murder suspect
item.description: Prosecutors on Monday sought the death penalty for a man accused of murdering a female high school student in the southwestern city of Gwangju in May, citing a high risk of repeat offenses. The Gwangju District Prosecutors Office demanded the sentence during the trial of 23-year-old Jang Yoon-gi, who was charged with killing 16-year-old Lee Chae-won on a street in Gwangju on May 5 after trying to rape her. Jang was also charged with attempting to kill a 17-year-old male student who had rushed to the scene to help the victim, raping a Vietnamese woman two days earlier and illegally filming a teenage girl's body in the past. "He poses a high risk of recidivism, including murder and sexual assault, in the event he returns to society," the prosecution said. Jang apologized to the victims in his final statement, saying he will pay for his crimes for the rest of his life. The sentencing hearing is scheduled to be held Sept. 30.

item.title: Bingo card for the soul: Seoul uses small steps to help people step outside
item.description: When one resident signed up for a municipal outdoor initiative earlier this summer, taking a walk in the rain was not part of the plan. But after checking off a challenge to visit a nearby neighborhood garden, the experience offered a rare moment of solace. “If not for the challenge, it’s a place I never would have stepped foot in,” the participant later recalled in a city survey. “Stepping out into the rain with an umbrella felt unexpectedly wonderful, and watching others enjoy their stroll made me realize I need to get out of the house far more often.” That quiet epiphany is precisely what municipal officials are aiming for. Facing a growing national crisis of social disconnection and loneliness — a phenomenon exacerbated by rapid urbanization and changing family structures — the Seoul Metropolitan Government is leaning into a gamified strategy to coax isolated residents back into public spaces. City authorities announced Monday the second phase of the "365 Seoul Challenge," an initiative designed to ease chronic feelings of loneliness by transforming everyday outdoor act

item.title: SK hynix still reviewing feasibility of Japan semiconductor plant
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said Monday that SK hynix is still reviewing the possibility of establishing a joint venture semiconductor plant in Japan, amid reports that the Korean chipmaker is considering building a facility in the neighboring country. On the sidelines of a meeting between representatives of the Korean and Japanese chambers of commerce in Sendai, Chey was quoted as saying, “We are in the process of studying it, and as soon as we finish, I will let you know,” when asked whether SK hynix would invest in Japan to build a chip production facility or establish a joint venture with a Japanese company to produce memory chips. However, Chey left without providing further details on potential sites in Japan, whether the plant would be built as a joint venture or who the potential partner might be. SK hynix is pursuing overseas expansion while continuing to invest in Korea. On Thursday, the company broke ground for an advanced high-bandwidth memory packaging fab in West Lafayette, Indiana. item.title: Seoul unveils first-ever autumn night festival map
item.description: When the autumn sun sets over the Han River, the capital’s urban centers usually rely on bright neon storefronts and late-night eateries to fuel the city's nightlife. This season, municipal authorities are taking charge of the nocturnal landscape, launching an ambitious cultural campaign designed to turn the evening hours into economic engines. The Seoul Metropolitan Government released its updated seasonal "Seoul Festival Map," detailing a lineup of events from September through November. For the first time, city planners have carved out a dedicated "Night Festival" category. The strategic pivot aims to expand evening leisure choices for residents after work while extending tourist stay times to inject foot traffic into local neighborhood businesses. The initiative comes as local governments across Korea seek new avenues to boost domestic spending and support small merchants recovering from persistent economic headwinds. item.title: Pikachu in hanbok: Pokémon powers up Korea's regional tourism drive
item.description: For millions of pop-culture enthusiasts around the world, catching ’em all is a lifelong pursuit. Now, Korea’s tourism authorities are betting that the world’s highest-grossing media franchise can help them capture the interest of a few million more international visitors. The Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) signed a formal partnership with Pokémon Korea, Monday, to harness the global megabrand for regional travel promotion. By pairing Nintendo’s iconic pocket monsters with local cultural sites, officials hope to disperse tourist traffic beyond the heavily trodden streets of the capital and into the country's lesser-visited provinces. The centerpiece of the collaboration aligns with "Pokémon Mega Festa 2026," a global celebration marking the 30th anniversary of the franchise's origin. From Sept. 18 through Oct. 11, HiKR Ground — the KTO's multi-story immersive travel center in central Seoul — will undergo a total Pokémon takeover. item.title: Foreign tourist arrivals up 21.3% through July, driven by Japanese visitors
item.description: Korea welcomed 12.8 million foreign tourists in the first seven months of 2026, a 21.3 percent increase from 10.56 million during the same period last year, the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Monday. Japanese travelers were a key driver. Through July, 28 percent of all Japanese people who traveled abroad chose Korea as their destination, the highest share on record and up 3.5 percentage points from a year earlier and outpacing the United States, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam as a destination for outbound travel. The number of Japanese visitors to Korea reached 2.28 million, up 18.8 percent, even as overall Japanese outbound travel grew at a more modest 4.1 percent to 8.14 million. Foreign tourist spending on credit and debit cards totaled 12.09 trillion won ($8.8 billion) through July, up 48.3 percent from 8.15 trillion won a year earlier. item.title: Prosecutors seek 10-year sentence for Pakistani man in child rape case
item.description: Prosecutors have sought a heavy sentence for a Pakistani national indicted for sexually assaulting foreign children nearly two decades earlier at an Islamic mosque in Incheon, west of Seoul, judicial officials said Monday. Prosecutors asked the Bucheon branch of the Incheon District Court to sentence the unidentified Pakistani man to 10 years in prison on charges including rape of minors under the age of 13, during a hearing in mid-July, the officials said. The man is accused of threatening and sexually assaulting two foreign children, then aged 7 and 9, at a mosque in Incheon's Seohae district in September 2008. He was teaching the Quran at the mosque at the time. Prosecutors said a complaint was filed belatedly because the victims were too young at the time of the incident.

item.title: What to expect as China's Xi Jinping attends SCO summit in Bishkek
item.description: As Washington’s strategic focus shifts and energy and grain supply disruptions continue to unsettle the Middle East, Beijing’s expanding presence across Central Asia is expected to be in focus as Kyrgyzstan hosts the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit this week. Chinese President Xi Jinping’s presence in Bishkek is expected to put the spotlight on whether the increasingly diverse grouping can move beyond diplomatic signalling, according to analysts. The SCO’s 25th anniversary summit was also expected to offer crucial clues to Beijing’s ambitions for a more multipolar Eurasia at a time of shifting regional power dynamics, they said. item.title: Cabinet reshuffle falls short of expectations for changes: experts
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung’s reshuffle of six ministers is largely viewed as a measure to gain momentum for his policies in his second year in office, as his support rates have declined significantly in response to public dissatisfaction with policies directly linked to people's livelihoods, like real estate and stock prices. This measure, however, is unlikely to produce the desired results, as political analysts say the personnel replacements are unlikely to help regain public support because they do not signal tangible policy changes. On Sunday, Cheong Wa Dae announced the replacement of ministers in six key posts — finance and economy; national defense; justice; SMEs and startups; gender equality and family; and land, infrastructure and transport. While experts differed on the finer points, many agreed the shake-up was intended to reset the political mood as Lee's approval rating continues falling. item.title: Ieodo seminar to discuss maritime security threats, cooperation in East Asia
item.description: The 10th Ieodo International Seminar will bring together experts in maritime security and international law on Jeju Island from Sept. 10 to 12 to discuss growing security threats and cooperation in East Asia. The Society of Ieodo Research, a Jeju-based think tank, and The Korea Times are jointly are hosting the three-day seminar in Jeju City under the theme “Maritime Security Cooperation Strategies among East Asian Countries: Responding to Intensifying Maritime Security Threats.” This year’s seminar will examine emerging maritime security challenges in East Asia and explore avenues for strengthening regional cooperation and developing effective responses grounded in international law. The opening session will feature a keynote from Chung Kee-yong, special representative for the Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The session will examine gray-zone threats and maritime security responses in East Asia, focusing on the growing use of coercive measures below the threshold of armed conflict and their implications for regional maritime security. item.title: KOSPI reverses losses as Samsung, SK hynix buybacks lift sentiment
item.description: The benchmark KOSPI rebounded from a steep opening drop to close higher, Monday, as share buybacks by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix lifted the index amid concerns over a potential U.S. interest rate hike in September. The won continued to strengthen, closing in the 1,360-won range against the dollar for the first time in 13 months. The KOSPI closed at 6,820.02, up 0.46 percent from the previous session. The index opened 2.58 percent lower but gained momentum as large-cap stocks rebounded broadly in afternoon trading. Foreign investors sold a net 640 billion won ($467 million) worth of shares, while institutions offloaded a net 793 billion won. Retail investors were also net sellers, unloading 144 billion won. Corporate investors net purchased 1.57 trillion won, absorbing much of the selling pressure. They extended their net-buying streak on the KOSPI to nine sessions. item.title: Seoul Jewelry Week returns with AI-powered styling pop-up, runway show tied to fashion week
item.description: More than 100 Seoul-based jewelry brands are taking part in "Seoul Jewelry Week 2026," a citywide promotional event running Sept. 1-15 that includes storewide discounts, a runway show, an AI-powered styling pop-up and industry seminars, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said. Now in its 11th year, the event is organized through the Seoul Jewelry Support Center, a city-run platform based in Jongno District's Seosulla-gil area — a historic jewelry-making district — that helps small and mid-sized jewelry brands with design, branding and market access, the government said. As part of the event, 80 Seoul-based jewelry brands are offering discounts and gifts with purchase at their stores and online shops through Sept. 15 under a joint promotion called "Ring Week in Seoul," with details available on the event's official website (jewelryweek.co.kr). From Tuesday through Sunday, coinciding with Seoul Fashion Week, a pop-up and runway show will run at Dongdaemun Design Plaza's B the B, a lifestyle space operated by the Seoul Business Agency. item.title: Supreme Court rules Korea Zinc's SMC-based restriction of Young Poong's voting rights 'unlawful'
item.description: The Supreme Court upheld a lower court ruling that Korea Zinc unlawfully restricted the voting rights of its largest shareholder, Young Poong, in a decision that could affect the fair trade watchdog's ongoing review of the smelter, observers said Monday. In a ruling issued Friday, the Supreme Court upheld the lower court's finding that Sun Metals Corp. (SMC), Korea Zinc's Australian affiliate, does not qualify as a subsidiary under the Korean Commercial Act. The top court found no error in the lower court's conclusion that SMC cannot be regarded as the same as, or most similar to, a stock company under Korean law. The dispute centers on Korea Zinc's use of SMC ahead of its extraordinary shareholders meeting in January 2025. Shortly before the meeting, SMC acquired about 10 percent of Young Poong's shares. Korea Zinc then argued that the resulting cross-shareholding relationship allowed it to restrict Young Poong's voting rights at the meeting. item.title: HYBE chairman to be referred to prosecution over alleged deception of shareholders: police
item.description: Bang Si-hyuk, chairman of K-pop powerhouse HYBE, will be referred to the prosecution this week for possible indictment on suspicion of deceiving investors into selling their stakes in his company, police said Monday. "We plan to forward the case to the prosecution within the week," Hong Seok-ki, head of the National Office of Investigation, told a press briefing. Bang is accused of violating the Capital Markets Act by deceiving investors into selling their stakes in Hybe in 2019, just before the company went public, making nearly 200 billion won ($145 million) in additional and illegal profits. Police launched an investigation into the allegations in December 2024 and began a full-scale probe in July of last year, which included a raid on Hybe headquarters. Their investigation was prolonged after the prosecution requested supplementary investigations while rejecting two arrest warrant requests filed by the police. Sources close to the issue said the police were expected to refer Bang's case to the prosecution without seeking his detention.

item.description: Foreign customers' purchases at health and beauty retailer CJ Olive Young surpassed 1 trillion won ($727.5 million) at its domestic stores in the first eight months of this year, reaching the milestone three months earlier than last year, while also seeing international visitors at its locations beyond Seoul. CJ Olive Young said Monday that cumulative purchases by foreign customers at its offline stores from January to August exceeded 1 trillion won, reaching the milestone earlier than last year when it achieved equivalent sales in November. The company recorded 11.01 million transactions by foreign customers during the period, or roughly one transaction every 0.9 seconds during store operating hours. The development underscores how K-beauty retailers are increasingly becoming part of tourism infrastructure, rather than simply a shopping stop in Seoul’s popular districts. Foreign customers accounted for 33 percent of Olive Young’s total offline store sales as of August, up from 2 percent in 2022, according to the company. item.description: SK On, the battery-making unit of Korea’s SK Innovation, said Monday it has signed a long-term deal to supply battery cells for energy storage systems (ESS) to U.S. company NeoVolta Power. Under the five-year deal, SK On will supply a total of 9 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pouch cells from 2027 to 2031. The batteries will be produced at SK On’s plant in Georgia. The companies did not disclose the value of the deal, but market estimates put it at about 1.5 trillion won ($1.09 billion). The deal is expected to help SK On secure a stable customer for its ESS batteries in the United States and increase production at its local facilities. SK On has been expanding into the ESS market as demand for EV batteries has slowed. The company has mainly focused on high-nickel EV batteries but is now adding LFP batteries, which are widely used in ESS due to their lower cost and longer life. NeoVolta Power selected SK On as a key battery supplier, citing the Korean firm’s battery technology and U.S. production capabilities. The two companies also plan to expand their partners

item.title: Korea steps up checks on Chinese cabbage, kimchi amid formaldehyde scare
item.description: Korean authorities have intensified safety checks on imported Chinese cabbage and kimchi — staples of Korean cuisine — after a Chinese supplier was found to have used formaldehyde, a known human carcinogen, to extend the shelf life of harvested cabbages. Central and local authorities say they have strengthened inspections at ports of entry while expanding testing for the chemical and other potentially harmful substances in food ingredients from China. On Monday, Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon visited the city-run Seoul Research Institute of Public Health and Environment to observe the testing process, including sample preparation and detailed laboratory analysis of Chinese cabbage and cabbage kimchi collected for screening. “Public anxiety over Chinese food ingredients has grown significantly following the discovery of a case in which formaldehyde was used in Chinese cabbage kimchi,” Oh said. “We will use this opportunity to strengthen regular inspections — not only for formaldehyde, but also to determine whether Chinese food ingredients are exposed to heavy metals, artificial color

item.title: Dongwon F&B launches health-focused Chuseok gift sets
item.description: Dongwon F&B has launched more than 110 types of gift sets for this year’s Chuseok holiday, expanding offerings centering on protein, reduced-sugar products and eco-friendly packaging. The major food company said Monday it increased the number of tuna can gift set varieties by 20 percent in response to growing consumer interest in protein. The lineup includes sets featuring Dongwon Tuna’s high-protein Light Standard product, which contains 25 grams of protein in a 135-gram can, nearly half the 55-gram recommended daily protein intake for adults. Dongwon F&B will also offer sets combining flavored tuna products, including spicy and vegetable tuna, as well as gift sets containing two new Super Tuna products. Available through online shopping malls, the products include Protein 30, which contains 30 grams of protein, and low-sodium albacore tuna, which contains 70 percent less sodium, according to the company. item.title: [COVER STORY] Lee bets on same economic playbook despite Cabinet reshuffle
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung is betting on the same economic playbook despite his Cabinet reshuffle, with career bureaucrats tapped to lead the ministries overseeing economic and housing policies, analysts said Monday. Lee on Sunday nominated Lee Hyoung-il, currently the first vice finance minister, for finance minister, and Hong Jee-sun, currently the second vice minister of land, infrastructure and transport, to lead the ministry. The two were among six ministerial nominees announced in the reshuffle. The changes come as both economic and housing policies have faced growing public criticism. The departures of Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol and Land Minister Kim Yun-duk were widely viewed as dismissals, with public sentiment turning against the Lee administration following the tax reform package and housing supply plans unveiled earlier this month. However, the president's choice of replacements suggests that he is seeking to reinforce rather than overhaul his policy direction. item.title: Korea's biz lobby group chief calls for stronger economic ties with Japan
item.description: The head of Korea's major business lobby group on Monday stressed the need for closer economic cooperation with Japan, saying the two countries share many similarities and can serve as partners in expanding each other's markets. Chey Tae-won, chairman of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI), made the remarks in his opening speech at a meeting with his Japanese counterpart held in Sendai, Japan. Chey said such efforts are crucial as Korea and Japan face a rapidly changing global economic environment and share similarities. "Korea and Japan have many similarities in terms of their industrial structures, markets and technologies," Chey said. "The strengths of one country can make up for the weaknesses of the other." Chey, who also heads Korea's SK Group which includes chipmaker SK hynix Inc., emphasized the importance of jointly building a larger market and industrial ecosystem. "That is what I consider economic solidarity between Korea and Japan," he said. item.title: Seoul Plaza turns into after-work fitness hub
item.description: Seoul Plaza is set to become an after-work fitness hub this fall, offering free evening classes for residents looking to trade the commute home for a workout in the heart of the city. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday that its “Exercising Seoul Plaza” program will begin Tuesday and run through Oct. 29, with 10 sessions combining group workouts, personalized exercise consultations and fitness challenges. The program will generally take place at 7 pm, giving office workers and other residents an opportunity to exercise without traveling far from their daily routines. Classes will include stretching, nighttime diet dance, bodyweight training and barre, which combines elements of ballet and Pilates. Participants will also be able to receive one-on-one consultations from trainers, posture-correction specialists and physical therapists through a program called the Exercise Prescription Center. item.title: Seoul finds harmful substances in 7 children's products
item.description: Products marketed for children 14 and older are drawing scrutiny after Seoul officials had safety concerns or found harmful substances in seven of 20 products tested. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that its testing found excessive levels of phthalate plasticizers, cadmium and other substances in sensory toys, stickers and keycap key rings sold through overseas online platforms and domestic stationery stores. The products were labeled for users 14 and older, meaning they were not subject to mandatory certification, but officials compared their safety results with standards applied to products intended for children ages 8 and older. Three of five sensory products tested contained phthalate plasticizers at levels as high as 164.2 times the relevant children’s product standard, while packaging for one product contained phthalates at 142.7 times the standard and cadmium at 1.5 times the limit. Two products also exceeded reference limits in tests designed to determine whether substances could leach from products, with formaldehyde reaching 2.3 times the limit, methanol 1.3 ti

item.title: N. Korea denounces US hostile policy toward it, vows 'toughest' response
item.description: North Korea on Monday denounced the United States for maintaining what it called a "hostile" policy and vowed to respond with the "toughest" countermeasures. North Korea's response came after the U.S. Department of State reaffirmed Washington's commitment to the "complete" denuclearization of Pyongyang, though U.S. President Donald Trump has expressed hope to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un later this year. In a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), a spokesperson at North Korea's foreign ministry said the U.S. continues to pursue "hostile" measures under the banner of denuclearization and human rights. item.title: Fair trade watchdog approves Hanwha's acquisition of additional KAI stakes
item.description: Korea's fair trade watchdog on Monday approved Hanwha Group's recent acquisition of additional stakes in Korea Aerospace Industries Ltd. (KAI). The Fair Trade Commission's (FTC) approval came after Hanwha Systems recently purchased a 3.45 percent stake in KAI, raising Hanwha Group's combined stake in the aircraft manufacturer to 15.89 percent, including the 9.9 percent held by Hanwha Aerospace. "KAI's largest shareholder is the Export-Import Bank of Korea, with a 26.41 percent stake, while the National Pension Service holds 8.75 percent," the FTC said. "At this stage, we have concluded that Hanwha Group's 15.89 percent stake is not sufficient to exercise substantial influence over KAI's overall management," the watchdog said. The FTC, however, noted that it would conduct another merger review if Hanwha becomes KAI's largest shareholder, or if Hanwha executives concurrently account for at least one-third of KAI's executives. item.title: Can humans really fall in love with AI? Korean dating show looks for answers
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become deeply embedded in everyday life, quickly organizing information and taking care of tedious tasks. An experiment is now taking that relationship a step further, exploring whether AI can become a romantic partner. SBS’s “My AI Partner — Strange Love” asks whether people can fall in love with when there is no person and no physical presence on the other end. The show follows celebrities as they date AI "partners" to explore whether an emotional connection is possible. Beyond simply testing whether people can form relationships with AI, it examines whether those relationships can evoke the same feelings that arise between people. It also asks how far AI’s role can expand as the technology finds its way into more aspects of everyday life. The first episode begins with cast members Jang Do-yeon and Kian84 meeting their AI partners for the first time. At first, their awkwardness is apparent as they talk to the AI on their tablets. Conversations sometimes veer off track because the AI is too passive or fails to grasp the context. Even its affe

item.description: The main opposition People Power Party (PPP) on Monday criticized President Lee Jae Myung's latest Cabinet reshuffle, accusing him of putting his political interests before improving people's livelihoods. Lee tapped six ministers in a major reshuffle on Sunday, including Rep. Kim Seung-won of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) as the new justice minister and Rep. Yong Hye-in, floor leader of the minor Basic Income Party, as the new gender equality minister. "This Cabinet reshuffle is President Lee's declaration that he is completely rejecting public calls for an overhaul of state affairs," PPP floor leader Jeong Jeom-sig said during a meeting of the party's supreme council at the National Assembly. Rep. Jeong particularly took issue with Kim's nomination as justice minister, arguing that it was intended to help drop criminal charges against the president. item.title: SK Telecom turns everyday photos into searchable AI records
item.description: Photos taken in passing can become difficult to find when they are needed most, but SK Telecom is introducing a feature designed to turn those snapshots into searchable records. SK Telecom said Monday it is launching A. log, a feature in its A. app that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to organize photos taken with Meta AI glasses and Android smartphones. The feature analyzes information in photos and automatically generates titles, descriptions and tags, allowing users to retrieve images by time or keywords. Photos can be automatically sorted into categories including business cards, receipts, whiteboards, meeting materials, parking locations and posters. For example, a user who photographs a concert poster can later search for the event using details such as its name, date or location rather than scrolling through a photo library. Users of Meta AI glasses can connect photos through the A. app by enabling automatic synchronization in A. log. SK Telecom said the feature works with all Meta AI glasses models, including Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2. Android smartphone users can also take pictures th

item.title: Rescue efforts intensify after Nepal-Tibet flooding as deaths climb past 900
item.description: KATHMANDU, Nepal — Rescuers were trying to find trapped workers in at least a dozen hydroelectric plant sites Monday after catastrophic flooding in Nepal and Tibet killed at least 900 people and left more than 4,700 missing. Multiple foreign teams were assisting local rescuers to find workers in multiple tunnels at Nepal's power plants on the rivers that flooded last Wednesday. Mohan Kumar Dangi, president of the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal, or IPPAN, said the floods damaged at least 12 hydropower projects across Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts and about 900 people were missing from the project sites. Officials have previously offered varying estimates of the number trapped. “We are working in search and rescue of the stranded people from hills, settlements and river areas,” said Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal’s army spokesman. Nepal’s disaster agency said Monday that 903 deaths had been counted in that country, with 4,247 people, including 592 foreigners, missing. item.title: Cause of death unknown for woman in Jeju missing person case: police
item.description: The exact cause of death remains unknown for a missing woman who was recently found dead on the southern resort island of Jeju due to body decomposition, a senior police official said Monday. The body of the victim, identified by her surname Jang, was discovered last Monday at a palm tree farm near an accommodation facility she had stayed at, months after she was first reported missing by her boyfriend in May. The case has faced intense scrutiny after a police officer was found to have closed her case without confirming her safety. The officer allegedly lied to the boyfriend that he had spoken with her and that he was asked not to share her location. "Due to the decomposition of her body, the cause of death is unknown," Hong Seok-ki, head of the National Office of Investigation, told reporters in a briefing. "We are investigating by leaving all possibilities open." Investigators earlier downplayed the likelihood of foul play, citing initial autopsy findings that suggested the victim died by hanging. item.title: Musinsa enters Malaysia, expands partnership with Indonesia's MAP
item.description: Musinsa, a Korean fashion and beauty platform operator, has signed an exclusive distribution agreement to bring its in-house clothing brand Musinsa Standard into Malaysia — its fourth market in Southeast Asia after the Philippines, Indonesia and Vietnam. The company said Monday it signed the deal with PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk, commonly known as MAP, the Indonesian retail conglomerate with which Musinsa struck a similar exclusive distribution agreement for Indonesia last month. Musinsa said it chose to expand its partnership with MAP because of the company's retail experience and distribution networks in both countries, and said it would look for further business synergies between the two markets. Malaysia is one of Southeast Asia's major fashion markets, with a large base of consumers with strong purchasing power and well-developed shopping infrastructure, including large malls in the capital, Kuala Lumpur, Musinsa said. item.title: Gov't team begins ground search for 9 missing Koreans in Nepal floods
item.description: A government joint rapid response team on Monday began a ground search for nine Koreans missing in massive floods in Nepal, while continuing to seek permission from Nepali authorities to operate helicopters, Seoul's foreign ministry said. The team plans to make its way to Ramche, about 1-2 kilometers from the site where the nine Koreans went missing, and camp there overnight, according to the ministry. The team includes officials from the ministry, police and fire authorities, and was dispatched to Nepal last week to support rescue efforts. The ground search began after the team failed to secure helicopter clearance due to bad weather and a decision by Nepalese authorities to bar foreign helicopters from operating. "As we did not receive helicopter clearance Sunday, some team members left by road and moved as close as possible to the accident site," a ministry official said. "After taking the overall situation at the site into consideration, we determined that a ground search would be possible." The team also plans to conduct a drone search in the area, subject to approval from local auth

item.title: Korean beef exports to Hong Kong expand under eased quarantine rules
item.description: Korean beef exporters are set to regain access to Hong Kong from parts of Gyeonggi Province and North Gyeongsang Province after Seoul and Hong Kong agreed to narrow restrictions imposed when foot-and-mouth disease is detected. The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs said Monday that the revised quarantine rules will take effect Tuesday, allowing export restrictions to be imposed at the city and county level rather than across an entire province. The change means Korean beef from areas including Anseong in Gyeonggi Province and Gyeongju and Goryeong in North Gyeongsang Province can return to the Hong Kong market after exports were halted following disease outbreaks. Gyeonggi and North Gyeongsang exported 11 tons of Korean beef worth $680,000 to Hong Kong in 2025, accounting for 22 percent of Korea’s total beef exports to the territory. item.source:markdown: Korean beef exporters are set to regain access to Hong Kong from parts of Gyeonggi Province and North Gyeongsang Province after Seoul and Hong Kong agreed to narrow restrictions imposed when foot-and-mouth disease is detected. The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs said Monday that the revised quarantine rules will take effect Tuesday, allowing export restrictions to be imposed at the city and county level rather than across an entire province. The change means Korean beef from areas including Anseong in Gyeonggi Province and Gyeongju and Goryeong in North Gyeongsang Province can return to the Hong Kong market after exports were halted following disease outbreaks. Gyeonggi and North Gyeongsang exported 11 tons of Korean beef worth $680,000 to Hong Kong in 2025, accounting for 22 percent of Korea’s total beef exports to the territory. item.title: Korea, US agree to expand cooperation in nuclear, high-energy physics
item.description: Government officials from Korea and the United States met in Washington, D.C., last week and agreed to expand cooperation in the area of nuclear and high-energy physics, Seoul's science ministry said Monday. Koo Hyuk-chae, first vice minister of science and ICT, signed a statement of interest (SOI) on such a partnership with Dario Gil, the under secretary for science at the U.S. department of energy, on Thursday (U.S. time), the ministry said in a press release. Under the agreement, the two countries will identify areas of cooperation in large-scale research infrastructure, while also promoting partnerships in computational science applications. A joint quantum cooperation committee will be established to implement such an agreement, the science ministry added. Koo also met with U.S. Chief Technology Officer Ethan Klein to discuss the progress on a working group aimed at implementing the technology prosperity deal signed between the two countries last October. item.title: Naver-Kurly grocery venture reports 10-fold rise in 1st-year transactions
item.description: Kurly N Mart, an online grocery service launched jointly by Naver and Kurly, saw its transaction volume surge tenfold in its first year, driven by loyal subscribers from Naver’s paid membership program, the companies said Monday. The service launched in September 2025, combining Naver's broad base of online shopping users and its Naver Plus Store app with Kurly's product sourcing and dawn delivery network, a same-day pre-dawn delivery system Kurly pioneered in Korea's grocery delivery market. Naver said users in their 30s and 40s made up more than 72 percent of customers who used the service 10 or more times, with people in their 40s visiting at least once a week on average. More than 80 percent of Kurly N Mart's transactions came through the Naver Plus Store app, the company said. item.title: Director Yoon Ga-eun wins top honors for gender equality in Korean culture
item.description: Long before the Korean public started thinking about women being behind the camera as well as in front of it, creative pioneers were quietly reshaping the country’s cultural landscape from the margins. That enduring artistic leadership will take center stage Tuesday, as the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism joins the Women’s Cultural Network to honor 19 individuals and organizations at the 19th Gender Equality Cultural Awards at the National Library of Korea in Seoul. Established in 2008, the annual ceremony celebrates figures across arts, entertainment and athletics who have dismantled social stereotypes and championed gender equity. Director Yoon Ga-eun, acclaimed for her nuanced explorations of youth relationships and coming-of-age, was named "Cultural Person of the Year." Yoon, whose past films include "The World of Us" and her recent feature, "The Owner of the World," has consistently centered young women’s perspectives, examining how girls navigate identity, social prejudice and emotional growth on their own terms. item.title: 1 dead, 15 missing after Grand Canyon flash floods
item.description: FLAGSTAFF, Ariz. — One person died and about 15 people are missing or unaccounted for after a major flash flood at the Grand Canyon forced evacuations, swept large boulders into the Colorado River and knocked out the sole water pipeline that serves tourists and residents, the National Park Service said Sunday. The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, the park service said without providing additional details. Coroner’s officials were at the scene. Weekend flooding in Arizona’s Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, happened Saturday afternoon. More than 60 people were evacuated from the depths of the canyon. The park service said it had yet to account for 15 people and asked anyone with details about hikers or campers in the canyon to get in touch. The Arizona Department of Public Safety was helping with additional evacuations Sunday. Because the main water line was out of service, starting Monday tourists won't be able to stay overnight at lodges and hotels within Grand Canyon National Park. Year-round resid

item.title: NC AI takes physical AI to Saudi tech showcase
item.description: NC AI is taking its vision of physical artificial intelligence (AI) to Riyadh this week, where it will showcase technology designed to connect virtual environments with machines operating in the physical world. The Korean physical AI company said Monday it will operate a joint pavilion for the Korean Full-Stack AI Consortium at LEAP 2026, which runs Monday through Thursday at the Riyadh Exhibition and Convention Center. The four-day technology exhibition is expected to draw more than 201,000 visitors from 203 countries and feature more than 1,000 speakers, including AMD Chief Executive Lisa Su and physicist Michio Kaku. NC AI will join MegazoneCloud, Upstage, FuriosaAI and Uracle in presenting Korean capabilities spanning AI semiconductors, AI models, cloud and infrastructure. At its pavilion, NC AI will focus on VAETKI, its industry-specific AI technology, and demonstrate how physical AI can move from digital environments to real-world action. item.title: Immigration detainees lack access to key forms, rights information: watchdog
item.description: The state human rights watchdog has called for stronger procedural safeguards for foreign nationals in immigration detention after inspections found inadequate access to review and temporary release forms, as well as insufficient guidance on detainees’ rights. The National Human Rights Commission of Korea (NHRCK) said Monday it inspected the Seoul Immigration Office, the Hwaseong Immigration Detention Center and the Cheongju Immigration Detention Center to see how the revised Immigration Act has operated in the field since taking effect in June 2025. The revised law allows immigration officials to detain foreign nationals facing deportation for an initial period of up to two months. That period can be extended for three months at a time following review by a detention review panel. Detention is capped at a maximum of nine months, extendable to 20 months in cases such as delays in enforcement over refugee applications or violations of the National Security Act. item.title: Trump 2028? Even Trump has begun hinting it may not happen
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump has frequently suggested he wants to seek a third term , posting about mounting another campaign, donning 2028 caps and discussing ways to make it happen — even as he's acknowledged the Constitution prohibits it. But lately, Trump has begun showing signs that even he doesn't really believe another run will happen. During recent speeches, the Republican president has begun describing life after the White House when his term ends in January 2029, predicting he'll be at home and agonizing as his successor claims credit for his accomplishments. “Your next president is going to say, ‘What a great job I did,’” Trump told an event on Long Island, New York, this month. “He’ll be sitting around, watching television. A real stiff. Unless you vote Republican, of course.” A sitting president talking about becoming a former one is always politically fraught. item.title: Hanyang University pioneers new internationalization model, providing end-to-end support for int'l students
item.description: Hanyang University is stepping up internationalization efforts under its “Boundless, Passionate and Uncharted” vision. The university’s Office of International Admissions said the university has established a new model of internationalization that is boundless, driven by passion and growth, venturing into uncharted territory. The office added that the university has also set a goal of fostering shared growth in the internationalization of Korean higher education by pioneering this new model among Korean universities. “The new internationalization model goes beyond simply recruiting international students,” a university official said. “We provide end-to-end support spanning admissions, employment, entrepreneurship and settlement in Korea.” He noted that the university regards breaking down the boundaries of nationality, culture, roles and goals as the foundational principle of internationalization. item.title: Experiential travel drives Korea's tourism growth
item.description: When travelers book an overnight stay in Korea today, the real decisive factor is no longer the quality of the hotel room, but what lies beyond its front door. According to a comprehensive study released Monday by the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO), overnight stays across the country grew by 5.1 percent over the past three years. This expansion was overwhelmingly driven by foreign visitors, whose overnight stays surged by 29 percent — a growth rate 15 times that of domestic travelers (1.9 percent). While domestic tourists still account for 85.4 percent of total room nights, international travelers have emerged as the primary engine of industry growth. Using big data from telecommunications, credit card transactions and lodging platforms via its Data Lab initiative, the state-run agency revealed a fundamental shift in traveler behavior. Bookings for properties linked to external leisure experiences surged dramatically over the three-year period: golf-themed lodging reservations jumped nearly 200 percent, hot springs properties rose 98.9 percent and water park accommodations grew 56.

item.title: Seoul turns outdoor screens into citywide art gallery for Kiaf
item.description: Seoul will turn eight downtown media screens into a sprawling outdoor gallery next month, bringing works by four artists to commuters and visitors as Kiaf Seoul expands beyond its traditional home at COEX. The “Media Art Seoul × Kiaf” special exhibition will run from Tuesday through Sept. 19, with the same two-minute program playing simultaneously every hour at eight locations in and around Gwanghwamun. The works will appear on five privately operated outdoor screens, including KT Square, K-Vision at Koreana Hotel, Lumi Media, LUUX and Ilmin Museum of Art, as well as three city media platforms. The screens will operate from 6 a.m. to midnight, with the media facades at Atelier Nodeul and Atelier Gwanghwa running from 7 p.m. to 11 p.m. The four artists selected by the Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Galleries Association of Korea are JE BAAK, Seok Chang-woo, Jeon Hye-ju and Han Seung-gu. item.title: Trump says Iran's Kharg is being 'blown to smithereens', but gives no details
item.description: WASHINGTON — Iran's energy hub of Kharg Island is being blown to smithereens, U.S. President Donald Trump said on Sunday in a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video clip. There was no other evidence that the Iranian energy hub was under attack. The White House and the U.S. Defense Department did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours. There was no immediate response to Trump's post on Iranian media. "Kharg Island being blown to smithereens!!! President DJT," Trump said on social media, but gave no further details. Reuters confirmed that an accompanying video clip showing dramatic explosions was most likely synthetically-generated, using software that detects AI-manipulated imagery. Attacking Kharg, which handled 90 percent of Iran's oil exports before the war launched by U.S. and Israeli attacks on February 28, would severely disrupt its energy trade and put huge pressure on its economy. item.title: Stray Kids' Lee Know donates $72,000 for Nepal flood relief
item.description: Lee Know of the K-pop boy band Stray Kids donated 100 million won (about $72,000) to support relief efforts for people displaced by severe flooding in Nepal, his management agency, JYP Entertainment, said Monday. Lee Know delivered the donation on Aug. 28 to World Vision, an international humanitarian and development NGO, requesting that it go toward saving the lives of children and families affected by the flooding and helping them sustain their livelihoods. The funds will support food and nutrition assistance, temporary housing and clean water and sanitation programs for flood-affected residents. "I hope my gesture can offer even a small bit of strength to those going through a difficult time," Lee Know said in a statement released through JYP Entertainment. "I sincerely hope that both those displaced and everyone working on relief efforts can return to peaceful daily life as soon as possible." Lee Know has donated regularly to causes at home and abroad. item.title: Seoul to glow in champagne green for NCT's 10th anniversary
item.description: A decade after SM Entertainment launched its ambitious blueprint to reshape K-pop through unlimited global expansion, NCT is taking over the Korean capital for a monthlong festival celebrating its 10th anniversary. Throughout September, the powerhouse mega-group — encompassing distinct sub-units including NCT 127, NCT DREAM, WayV, NCT U and NCT WISH — will anchor a multi-disciplinary cultural takeover across Seoul. Blending live music, high fashion and public light installations, the festival marks 10 years since the brand debuted in 2016. Its experimental, open-member model, initially viewed as a risky structural departure in an industry historically built on fixed bands, has since established NCT as a dominant commercial pillar of modern popular culture. The public celebration kicks off along the Han River at Banpo Hangang Park, where the famous Moonlight Rainbow Fountain will execute daily water shows choreographed to the group’s biggest hits. item.title: University of Seoul's Startup Foundation participates in entrepreneurship support project
item.description: The University of Seoul’s Startup Foundation will help foster innovative entrepreneurs by taking part in the government’s large-scale entrepreneurship support program, according to the university. The university said the foundation has been selected for the second phase of the “Startup for All Project” funded by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups. The project is designed to support aspiring entrepreneurs with innovative ideas in pursuing their startup ambitions. A total of 10,000 entrepreneurs will be recruited for the second phase of the project, twice the number recruited for the first phase. The university noted that it will serve as a mentoring institution for the general and technology startup tracks, in which 8,000 prospective entrepreneurs will be selected. Selected entrepreneurs will receive government-backed benefits, including 2 million won ($1,448) in startup support funding and customized artificial intelligence (AI) solutions worth up to 1 million won for two months, as well as mentoring from experts. item.title: Prosecution-police team wraps up probe into political-religious collusion
item.description: A joint prosecution-police team investigating suspected collusion between politics and religion concluded its activities Monday, 237 days after its launch on Jan. 6. The team achieved notable results, including the arrest and indictment of Lee Man-hee, founder of the Shincheonji Church of Jesus, a nonmainstream religious sect, and the seizure of 26 billion won ($18.9 million) in cash from the private safe of Unification Church leader Han Hak-ja. The team had investigated allegations of Shincheonji coercing its members into joining the People Power Party (PPP), tax evasion and embezzlement of funds, as well as the Unification Church's illegal donation of political funds and embezzlement of church funds. Consequently, four Shincheonji officials, including Lee, were arrested and indicted, with 12 other officials indicted without detention. Lee and other church officials were accused of forcing church followers to join the PPP with the aim of influencing the results of various elections from 2021 to 2024. item.title: GS Retail fined $9.3 mil. over personal data leak of 1.66 mil. customers
item.description: GS Retail Co., a retail giant that operates GS25 convenience stores, has been issued a 12.8 billion-won ($9.3 million) fine over a personal data leak that affected 1.66 million customers, the privacy watchdog said Monday. According to the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC), an unidentified hacker infiltrated the company's home shopping platform GS SHOP and its convenience store chain between 2024 and 2025 by repeatedly injecting a large number of pre-secured user IDs and passwords to successfully bypass login systems. Through the member information modification pages, the hacker compromised the personal data of 1.58 million GS SHOP users and 79,128 GS25 customers. The leaked information included their names, gender, dates of birth, contact numbers, home addresses and email addresses. The privacy watchdog said GS Retail failed to notice abnormal signs, such as a sharp spike in login attempts and failures from identical IP addresses within a short time frame, which allowed the unauthorized access to persist undetected over a prolonged period. item.title: S. Korean ambassador to Moscow to attend Russia's economic forum
item.description: South Korea's ambassador to Russia will attend Russia's annual Eastern Economic Forum this week in Vladivostok, a foreign ministry official said Monday. Ambassador Lee Sok-bae, who took up the post in November, will attend the international forum, running from Tuesday to Friday, according to the official. The ambassadorial post was vacant during last year's edition of the annual event. Lee is said to have received an invitation to attend this year. This year's edition has drawn attention amid speculation that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un could travel to Russia for a possible summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the forum. Earlier in the day, Seoul's unification ministry said it had no plans to take part in the forum. On the chances of Kim's attendance, the unification ministry said it had no information on the matter but will keep monitoring the situation. item.title: Seoul district steps up housing protections for foreign tenants
item.description: Navigating the intricacies of Korea’s residential real estate market is notoriously complex even for long-term local residents. For the country’s steadily growing international population, however, steep language barriers, unfamiliar administrative procedures and unique tenant laws make securing rental housing a particularly daunting endeavor — and one fraught with potential financial risk. To help bridge this informational divide and protect vulnerable foreign renters, Gangbuk District, an administrative district in northeastern Seoul, is expanding a comprehensive municipal program designed to safeguard foreign residents throughout the housing lease process. Under the enhanced initiative, foreign tenants visiting local neighborhood centers to register their move-in address or file for an official "fixed date" status (hwakjeong ilja) will receive automated administrative guidance stamped directly onto their documentation in nine languages. The legal stamp — covering English, Chinese, Vietnamese, Mongolian, Filipino, Uzbek, Japanese, Taiwanese and Thai — outlines essential pro

item.title: Tax revenue up $6 bil. in July on higher wages, brisk stock trading
item.description: Korea's tax revenue rose by 8.4 trillion won ($6 billion) in July from a year earlier on higher collections of income and securities transaction taxes, data showed Monday. The government collected 51 trillion won in taxes last month, according to the Ministry of Finance and Economy. Income tax revenue rose by 1.8 trillion won to 13.6 trillion won. The finance ministry attributed the increase partly to higher wages and increased housing transactions. The country's bullish securities markets also contributed to the growth, with securities transaction tax collection rising by 1.1 trillion won to 1.4 trillion won. Value-added tax revenue increased by 3.2 trillion won to 24.6 trillion won due to growth in imports. For the January-July period, Seoul's tax earnings came to 274 trillion won, up a sharp 41.4 trillion won from a year earlier.

item.title: Hanwha Aerospace signs deal to export K9 howitzers to Spain
item.description: Korean defense company Hanwha Aerospace said Monday it has signed a deal with Spanish defense firm Indra Sistemas S.A. to export K9 self-propelled howitzers. In a regulatory filing, Hanwha Aerospace said it signed the contract with Indra without disclosing the contract value or delivery schedule, citing confidentiality. Under the contract, Hanwha Aerospace will receive an initial payment equivalent to 20 percent of the contract value after signing, followed by another 5 percent by the end of the year. The deal marks the first entry of Hanwha Aerospace's K9 into the Western European market, which would bring the number of countries operating the self-propelled howitzer to 11.

item.title: DAPA completes development of armored medical evacuation vehicle
item.description: The state arms procurement agency said Monday it has completed the development of an armored medical evacuation vehicle designed to increase the survivability of troops on the front lines. The armored vehicle was specially designed to help safely escort wounded soldiers on the front lines to hospitals while enabling them to receive remote medical support on the way, according to the Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA). Ambulances currently in use by the military have difficulty in providing emergency transport near combat units due to their low mobility and insufficient protection gears. DAPA plans to prepare for mass production of the medical evacuation vehicle to ensure timely delivery to the Army.

item.title: KTX expands Tuesday following SRT absorption
item.description: An integrated high-speed railway service integrating KTX and SRT trains will officially launch Tuesday, marking the first time the combined services will be available through a single dedicated platform. SRT trains, previously operated by SR, will join KTX services operated by KORAIL under the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. The integration of SR into KORAIL is intended to result in a major increase in seating capacity for passengers. The government said 15,000 additional seats will be available on weekdays and 17,000 on weekends. It also said the number of seats on routes departing from Suseo Station in southern Seoul will increase by 30 percent. Fares will be reduced by an average of 10 percent to match SRT pricing structures. Trips departing from Suseo Station will also now be eligible for mileage deals, usually equivalent to 5 percent of each ticket purchase. All trains will be available for booking through KORAIL+, the online platform launched by KORAIL in early August. The expanded KORAIL service will introduce 31 additional new trains next year, each with 500 seats

item.title: Oriental Brewery enters soju market with zero-sugar 'Charlang'
item.description: Oriental Brewery (OB), an AB InBev-owned brewer best known for its Cass beer brand, is entering Korea’s soju market for the first time with “Charlang,” a zero-sugar soju made with water from Jeju Island. The company said Monday that Charlang will hit the market in late September, marking a new chapter for OB as it expands beyond its core beer business. OB’s move into the soju business follows its acquisition of Jeju Soju from Shinsegae L&B, giving the company a foothold in the soju market and expanding its beverage portfolio beyond beer. Charlang is made with water sourced from eastern Jeju’s volcanic bedrock. OB said the water, naturally filtered through volcanic rock, gives the soju a milder taste, while sea salt adds a subtle savory note. The 15 percent alcohol-by-volume soju is designed to reduce the artificial aroma and sweetness found in some soju products, according to the company. item.title: T'way Air to operate as Trinity Airways from Sept. 10
item.description: T'way Air said Monday it will begin operating under its new name, Trinity Airways, on Sept. 10, completing its rebranding following its acquisition by leisure conglomerate Sono Trinity Group. The name change will be the Korean budget airline's first in 16 years and comes after Sono Trinity Group, formerly known as Daemyung Sono Group, took control of the carrier last year. The airline's flight codes and schedules, as well as existing reservations and terms of use, will remain unchanged after the name change. Sono Trinity Group acquired a 46 percent stake in T'way Air for 250 billion won ($176.4 million) in February 2025. The airline completed regulatory procedures in May to change its operating license to the new name.

item.title: Land minister nominee vows close consultations with Seoul on housing supply
item.description: The nominee to head the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport said Monday he will closely consult with the Seoul city government to narrow differences over housing supply plans. Hong Jee-sun, currently vice land minister, made the remarks a day after he was tapped to replace Land Minister Kim Yun-duk, who had faced opposition from the Seoul city government over a proposal to use parts of Yongsan Park in central Seoul for housing development. "I will hold sufficient consultations with the Seoul city government in advance to ensure that housing policies are effectively implemented," Hong told reporters on his way to the government complex in the administrative city of Sejong. Hong stressed the importance of cooperation between the central and local governments, citing his experience in housing and urban development policy at the Gyeonggi Provincial Government. "I will work to promptly supply quality housing in areas where people want to live, while paying particular attention to housing stability for young people and newlyweds," he said. The nominee is required to undergo a parliam

item.title: Gov't launches 2nd half program to recover remains of fallen Korean War soldiers
item.description: The defense ministry said Monday it has launched second-half operations to recover and identify the remains of soldiers killed in the 1950-53 Korean War, continuing its efforts to bring closure to families of service members killed in action or still missing. The Agency for KIA Recovery and Identification under the ministry will carry out the excavation project starting Monday through Nov. 27, deploying troops from 14 Army divisions and brigades, and the 1st Marine Division, the ministry said. The troops will be deployed to mountainous areas in more than 20 regions across Gyeonggi, Gangwon, South Chungcheong, North Jeolla and North Gyeongsang provinces. In particular, they plan to focus on the border areas of Paju, Cheorwon and the southeastern county of Gunwi, key battlegrounds against North Korean and Chinese communist forces at the height of the three-year conflict. item.title: Korea, US discuss energy cooperation amid heightened uncertainty
item.description: Energy officials from Korea and the United States discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the energy sector amid heightened global market uncertainties, Seoul's climate ministry said Monday. Korea's Second Vice Climate Minister Lee Ho-hyeon met with his U.S. counterpart, acting Assistant Secretary Curt Coccodrilli, in Seoul to discuss policy measures aimed at ensuring stable energy supply chains and power supplies, according to the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. They also exchanged views on key energy security issues that require a joint response, including ensuring the security of power grids amid rapidly growing electricity demand and expanding energy storage systems (ESSs), the ministry said. "Securing stable energy supply chains and power supplies is the backbone of a country's industrial competitiveness. We expect this meeting will help the two countries jointly respond to growing market uncertainties and strengthen bilateral energy cooperation," Lee said.

item.title: Seoul shares trim losses late Monday morning amid tech sell-off
item.description: Seoul shares trimmed earlier losses late Monday morning on retail buying, as hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh raised concerns over a possible interest rate hike next month. After opening 2.58 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) erased its losses, trading 133.62 points, or 1.96 percent, lower at 6,655.62 as of 11:20 a.m. Institutions and foreign investors sold a net 633.74 billion won ($460 million) and 474.72 billion won worth of stocks, respectively, while retail investors bought a net 502.09 billion won. In his first major speech since taking the helm of the Fed, Warsh warned that inflation is not slowing meaningfully, leaving the door open to further rate hikes at the annual Jackson Hole symposium in Wyoming on Friday. In addition to heightened bets on a U.S. rate hike, investors remained on alert amid escalating tensions in the Middle East following renewed U.S. strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. On Friday (U.S. time), the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.02 percent, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite declined 0.52 percent.

item.title: Unification Church leader sentenced to 2-year prison term in bribery case
item.description: A Seoul district court on Monday sentenced Unification Church leader Han Hak-ja to two years in prison in a bribery case where the religious group sought to secure favors from the administration of former President Yoon Suk Yeol. The Seoul Central District Court handed down the sentence for the 83-year-old after finding her guilty of involvement in giving luxury bribes to Yoon's wife, former first lady Kim Keon Hee, and handing illegal funds to a former lawmaker. The court also sentenced Yun Young-ho, a former head of the church's global headquarters, to six months in prison and handed down a suspended prison term to a former aide to Han, both of whom were indicted in connection with the case. After the ruling, the Unification Church released a statement apologizing for causing concern but said it could not accept the ruling, signaling its intent to appeal. In its ruling, the court convicted Han of violating the anti-graft law for her involvement in giving a luxury necklace and a Chanel bag to the former first lady while requesting favors for the church through an intermediary in July 20

item.title: Lee's approval rating falls below 40% for 1st time: poll
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating fell below the 40 percent mark for the first time since he took office in June last year, a survey showed Monday, amid public dissatisfaction over housing policy. According to the survey conducted by Realmeter and commissioned by the EKN newspaper among 2,509 respondents aged 18 and older, 38.9 percent gave a positive assessment of Lee's performance, down 1.3 percentage points from the previous week, while 58.7 percent gave a negative assessment, up 1.8 percentage points. Realmeter attributed the decline to growing public dissatisfaction over housing prices and controversy over the presidential office's refusal to appoint a Supreme Court justice nominee, as well as public distrust of the police following a missing woman incident on the southern island of Jeju. Earlier this month, Lee's office decided not to nominate one of two Supreme Court justice candidates recommended by the chief justice after the recommendations were made without prior consultations with the office. item.title: Industrial output flat in July; retail sales down, facility investment up
item.description: Korea's industrial output remained flat in July from a month earlier, data showed Monday, with retail sales losing ground, while facility investment advanced. Industrial production remained unchanged in July from a month earlier, according to data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. Output in the mining and manufacturing sector, a key pillar of the economy, edged up 0.2 percent on the back of the electronic component segment. The output in the automobile industry, on the other hand, fell 4.5 percent. Retail sales, a gauge of private spending, backtracked 2.4 percent over the period, led mostly by durable goods, including cars. Facility investment shot up 7.5 percent in July from a month earlier, the latest findings showed.

The output in the automobile industry, on the other hand, fell 4.5 percent. Retail sales, a gauge of private spending, backtracked 2.4 percent over the period, led mostly by durable goods, including cars. Facility investment shot up 7.5 percent in July from a month earlier, the latest findings showed.

item.description: ASHEVILLE, North Carolina — The U.S. Treasury Department is likely to unveil weekly new secondary sanctions aimed at increasing economic pressure on Iran, with an initial focus on banks, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Reuters on Sunday. After imposing penalties on the United Arab Emirates branches of Egypt's Banque Misr on Friday over alleged financial links to Iran, Bessent said in an interview that the next step may be cutting off an institution entirely from the dollar-based financial system. "We're starting with the banks, and we're telling the banks it's not okay to have Iranian money and to aid the regime." item.title: Iran retaliates after first US strikes in a month
item.description: TEHRAN — Iran attacked U.S. military targets in the Middle East on Monday in retaliation for the first American strikes on its territory in a month, in a fresh flare-up of the war that has engulfed the region. Tehran's powerful Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said they had responded to Sunday's American attack by striking two U.S. air bases with ballistic missiles in Washington-allied Jordan, causing "heavy damage." Jordan's army said it had intercepted eight missiles, without stating their origin. Tehran also claimed it targeted U.S. military personnel at an air base in the United Arab Emirates and shot down a U.S. drone over the Strait of Hormuz. The flurry of attacks came after the United States said Sunday it had attacked Iranian rocket launchers on the small island of Larak in the strategic shipping lane. Washington said its attacks were aimed at preventing Iran from placing more sea mines in the strait, days after the U.S. announced it had completed clearing explosives from the waterway.
