item.title: US strikes Iranian rocket launchers at Strait of Hormuz in first military action in weeks
item.description: WASHINGTON — U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in their first military action in a month on Sunday, breaking a lull in fighting during an intermittent war that has lasted more than six months. Iran swiftly vowed to retaliate for what it called a deadly attack. Forces with the Revolutionary Guard Corps were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait, according to Tim Hawkins, a spokesperson for the U.S. Central Command. The U.S. military last week completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes. Semiofficial news outlets in Iran reported sounds of explosions near Larak island on the strait. The Guard in a statement carried by Iran's state broadcaster noted “the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots.” A return to open conflict would be dangerous for the region, where Iran has targeted U.S. military bases and infrastructure in Gulf countries since the war began on Feb. 28. item.title: ENHYPEN claims 1st No. 1 on Billboard 200 with 'The Sin: Bliss'
item.description: The latest album from K-pop boy group ENHYPEN has debuted at No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard's main albums chart, earning the group its first chart-topper. Billboard said in a preview of this week's chart on Sunday (U.S. time) that the band's eighth EP, "The Sin: Bliss," took the top spot on the Billboard 200, ahead of Ella Langley's "Dandelion" and Olivia Rodrigo's "you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love." This marks the first time the group has reached No. 1 since its debut in November 2020. Before ENHYPEN, BTS, SuperM, Stray Kids, Ateez and Tomorrow X Together had reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 among K-pop boy groups. Among girl groups, BLACKPINK, NewJeans, TWICE and Katseye have taken the honor, while the original soundtrack album for Netflix's global hit animation "KPop Demon Hunters" had also led the chart. "The Sin: Bliss" marks the band's seventh album in the top 10, all achieved since 2022. The act had previously gone as high as No. 2, twice, with "The Sin: Vanish" in January and "Romance: Untold" in 2024. The Billboard 200 ranks the most popular albums of the week in the Unite

item.title: From fighting software piracy to protecting children with AI
item.description: A career spent tracking illegal activity online has taken on a new purpose in the age of artificial intelligence (AI). For nearly two decades, Choi Seung-hyun worked in software license compliance and anti-piracy, including stints with Adobe, Microsoft, the Business Software Alliance and PTC. Now, the DragonEyes CEO is using that experience to develop an AI agent designed to find harmful online content and help protect children. “My 20 years in software license compliance were a major inspiration for DragonEyes,” Choi told The Korea Times in an interview. “It started with a question I had as a compliance professional about how we could tackle harmful content online. That eventually led me to develop an AI agent.” The idea became personal in November 2025, when Choi read about a multinational game company in the United States facing investigations over its handling of harmful online content. item.title: Inside Seoul's rapidly growing urban running scene
item.description: Park Eun-kyung, a former running club leader, recently joined a group session around Gyeongbok Palace organized by On Your Mark, a specialized running brand. "The Gyeongbok Palace loop is 2.5 kilometers, making it perfect for a 5 km run with two laps, and the flat, beginner-friendly terrain is a huge plus. Being a popular landmark, it's especially beautiful at sunset. It's also great for discovering hidden gem-like neighborhood cafes myself," she shared. Fueled by social media workout check-ins, the "puppy run" has become a viral hit among younger runners. Using GPS tracking apps, runners map out the shape of a dog on a digital map. This creative "art run" sweeps through Seochon, Samcheong-dong and Gwanghwamun, with runners navigating the alleyways to outline detailed features like ears, a tail and legs. item.title: Kia salesman turns hobbies into secret for sales milestone
item.description: For Kim Hyong-su, a veteran salesman at Kia, some of the most important connections in his career were not made inside a showroom. Sometimes, customers find him on a soccer field. Other times, they meet him through one of his hobbies. Kim, a sales director at the carmaker, has achieved cumulative vehicle sales of 4,000 to become the firm’s 40th Grand Master — a title awarded to salesmen who achieve the sales figure. Kim said his long-running hobbies — including soccer and triathlon — have played an unexpected role in helping him build relationships with customers and sustain a career that has spanned more than three decades. “I get inquiries from people I have met through my hobbies when they find out that I work for Kia,” Kim said in a recent telephone interview. item.title: "We're Not Going Back": Ron Daniels on the Legacy of 1972 Gary Convention & 1963 March on Washington
item.description:
As Gary, Indiana, recovers from flooding and a two-week power outage, we also speak with Ron Daniels, president of the Institute of the Black World 21st Century, who discusses the city’s history as a site of Black struggle and organizing. In 1972, the city hosted the National Black Political Convention, which brought together thousands of activists to plan for increasing African American political power. Attendees included Coretta Scott King, Betty Shabazz, Jesse Jackson, Bobby Seale, Louis Farrakhan, Shirley Chisholm, Harry Belafonte and Amiri Baraka.

“It was one of the great gatherings in the history of Black people in this country,” says Daniels, who calls the current backlash to racial progress “the dying gasp of a system that needs a major overhaul.”

item.title: "Left Behind and Overlooked": Indiana Energy Company Left Majority-Black Gary Powerless for Weeks
item.description:
Thousands of residents recently spent two weeks without power in Gary, Indiana, following a storm that ripped through the majority-Black city. The blackout ground the city to a halt, trapping residents in their apartments, forcing the closure of many businesses and leading to fuel shortages at gas stations. Officials in Indiana estimate the storm might have caused up to $5 billion in damage in Gary and other communities.

“We’re still in the recovery phase, as we speak,” says Gary Mayor Eddie Melton, who underscores that “hardening the infrastructure” should be a priority for the NIPSCO utility company. “We’ve never seen wind this strong before. … They need to ensure that the utility grid system is going to sustain that type of wind.”

item.title: The Real Reason There's a Munitions Shortage? Too Many Wars & a Dysfunctional Pentagon: William Hartung
item.description:
Top U.S. military leaders have reportedly advised Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth against extending the war in Iran because ongoing operations in the Middle East have degraded the Pentagon’s ability to confront threats elsewhere. According to The Washington Post, the warnings appeared in a classified assessment for Hegseth prepared by the heads of the Army, Navy and Air Force and the four-star commanders overseeing U.S. operations throughout Europe, Asia and Latin America. This comes after multiple reports have revealed the U.S. is facing a critical munitions shortage, having used up much of its global stockpile of expensive missile systems during the war against Iran.

“The Pentagon is completely dysfunctional when it comes to fighting this kind of war,” says defense analyst William Hartung, principal adviser at the Project on Government Oversight. He says the U.S. policy establishment and the defense industry are less interested in effectiveness than in running a “money-making machine.”

item.title: "Catastrophe of Unimaginable Proportions": Nepal Flood Death Toll Tops 900; Near 5,000 Still Missing
item.source:markdown:
More than 900 people in Nepal are confirmed dead after a massive wall of water, mud and debris crashed through a Himalayan river valley on the border with Tibet. More than 4,200 people are missing in Nepal and hundreds more in Tibet. Families are searching hospitals for loved ones, and crews have buried hundreds of unidentified bodies in shallow graves. Rescue efforts are also underway for more than 900 hydropower workers, believed to be trapped in more than a dozen underground tunnels blocked by debris. The cause of the flash flooding is believed to have been the collapse of a glacier in the mountains, leading a wave of water, rocks and debris to carve its way through the valley.
“This is a catastrophe of unimaginable proportions,” says journalist Kunda Dixit, speaking to _Democracy Now!_ from the Nepalese capital of Kathmandu.
“We used to say that the glaciers are melting in the Himalaya. Now it seems like the mountains are cracking up,” says Dixit. “This has sort of redefined what global warming and climate change is doing, not just to Nepal and the Himalaya, but to the planet.”
item.author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)

item.title: Bishop celebrates centenary of first Catholic Mass in Svalbard, Norway
item.description:
Bishop Erik Varden of Trondheim and Apostolic Administrator of Tromsø celebrated a solemn Mass in Longyearbyen on Sunday, 30 August, to mark 100 years since the first Catholic Mass was celebrated in Svalbard, Norway. In his homily, Bishop Varden reflects on vulnerability and loneliness, calling Christians to rediscover a sound sense of reality and to bring Christ’s reconciliation, healing and friendship to those who are isolated and afraid.

item.title: At least 6 dead after ferry carrying nearly 270 capsizes off northern Cyprus
item.description: BODRUM, Turkey — At least six people have died after a ferry carrying nearly 270 passengers and crew capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus on Sunday, Turkish media reported. More than 172 people have been rescued, Prime Minister of Northern Cyprus Unal Ustel told Turkish state-run TRT news channel. The catamaran-style ferry was traveling from the port of Kyrenia, also known as Girne, in the breakaway north of ethnically divided Cyprus, to the Turkish port of Tasucu in Mersin province. The Turkish ambassador to Nicosia, Ali Murat Basceri, said there were some casualties, but did not specify how many, speaking to Turkey’s state-run TRT news channel. Many of the 259 passengers and eight crew members were rescued, Basceri said, adding that some were taken to hospital. Kyrenia Mayor Murat Senkul said the ship belonged to the Filo Denizcilik ferry company and sank off the coast of Diana beach on Cyprus’ northern coast. item.title: NASA launches Roman Space Telescope to explore hidden universe
item.description: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA’s newest crown jewel blasted off Sunday to hunt for planets around other stars, explore secret dark energy and survey the cosmos like never before. SpaceX launched the $4.3 billion Roman Space Telescope shortly after daybreak aboard a triple-the-fire-power Falcon Heavy rocket from Kennedy Space Center. Roman blazed toward an observation point 1.6 million kilometers away that's home to the Webb Space Telescope, one of NASA's other big-ticket eyes in the sky. The bus-sized telescope — named after the late Nancy Grace Roman, NASA’s first chief astronomer — will take more than three months to reach its destination. Once there, it will cast the widest gaze yet on the hidden parts of the universe from space, uncovering the unimaginable with unsurpassed speed. “It’s going to find thousands of supernovae, tens of thousands of planets, billions of galaxies and tens of billions of stars,” NASA science mission director Nicky Fox said. “It’s going to be able to do things that we’ve never been able to do before with its massive field of view.” Sever

item.title: Tropical storm Karina strengthens into hurricane in Pacific, threatens major damage this week
item.description: MIAMI — Tropical Storm Karina strengthened into a hurricane in the Pacific Ocean on Sunday and could become a major storm this week, forecasters said. The cyclone's center was at far out sea and was not threatening land. Karina had maximum sustained winds of 80 miles per hour (130 kilometers per hour), the Miami-based National Hurricane Center said, making it a Category 1 hurricane. A major hurricane is Category 3 or greater. The storm was located about 820 miles southwest of the southern tip of Mexico’s Baja California Peninsula and was moving and was moving northwest at 15 miles per hour a forecast path farther out into the Pacific. While Karina was expected to stay well away from land, swells from the storm were likely to cause dangerous surf and rip current conditions along parts of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula, the hurricane center said. Elsewhere in the Pacific, Tropical Storm Lowell was 1,150 miles southeast of Hawaii, and it too posed no threat to land. item.title: 81% of Koreans want to marry, compared to 58% of Japanese: survey
item.description: More than 80 percent of young Koreans are interested in marriage compared with just 57.6 percent of young Japanese singles, a survey showed Sunday. The poll was conducted on 2,000 Koreans and 2,000 Japanese aged 20 to 39 from June to July, and found that 81.4 percent of the surveyed Koreans were interested in marriage, according to a bilateral committee dealing with promoting regional growth and tackling low birth rates and aging societies. The committee was launched on the occasion of a Korea-Japan summit last year and is co-headed by the chiefs of each country's Chamber of Commerce & Industry. According to the survey, 18.6 percent of Koreans had no interest in ever getting married, while the percentage among Japanese was 42.4 percent. As the ideal number of children, two was the most popular choice among Koreans at 52.6 percent, followed by one at 17 percent and three or more at 7.3 percent. Among Japanese, two was the most popular at 28.9 percent followed by three or more at 12.2 percent and one at 9.4 percent. As conditions for marriage, the most popular answer was one's own and his or

item.title: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan to hold first defense pact meeting, source says
item.description: ISTANBUL — Top officials from Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan will gather in Istanbul on Monday for a first committee meeting under the joint defense accord that they signed this month, a Turkish foreign ministry source said. The "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement," signed on Aug. 7, brought together Sunni Muslim U.S. allies concerned by the Iran war and regional conflict that has led to Iranian missile fire on Gulf oil exporters. It is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression and stipulates that an armed attack against any of the three would be regarded as an attack on all, similar to NATO's Article 5 collective defense clause. Foreign and defense ministers, as well as the chiefs of staff, of the three countries will attend the meeting in Istanbul, the ministry source said. "International security issues will be on the agenda," the source said, with discussions expected to cover enhancing defense capabilities, greater interoperability among their armed forces and deepening cooperation in the defense industry, including joint production and development. item.title: PM orders thorough readiness against heavy rain
item.description: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook instructed relevant agencies Sunday to make thorough preparations against damage from heavy rains forecast for this week. Noting that heavy rain is forecast for early Monday morning, Han called for establishing safety measures against additional damage in areas that have already been hit hard by earlier rains, according to her office. She particularly called for taking preemptive measures in damage-prone areas, such as slopes, run-down houses and retaining walls in residential neighborhoods. Additionally, she instructed officials to devise evacuation plans and give swift evacuation orders using all available resources in the event of danger.

item.title: 'The Odyssey' overtakes 'Spider-Man' as Korea's top overseas movie of 2026
item.description: Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" has become the highest-grossing foreign film released in Korea this year, surpassing "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" in a box office race that had been running neck and neck for weeks. As of Sunday, "The Odyssey" has drawn 8,471,082 admissions, according to the Korean Film Council, edging out "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," which had previously held the title of top-earning foreign film of 2026 here. Nolan's film crossed the 8 million mark on Friday, just 24 days after its release, faster than "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," which took 26 days to reach the same milestone, and set the record for the fastest run to 8 million box office sales among this year's releases. It has held the top spot in advance ticket sales for 28 consecutive days starting two days before its release, and has topped the daily box office every single day since its Aug. 5 debut, a 25-day streak that shows no signs of breaking. The film's success defies almost every recent trend in the Korean box office. Annual movie attendance remains far below pre-pandemic levels amid the rise of streaming

item.title: Korea employs helicopters for 2nd day to search for 9 missing nationals following massive flood
item.description: The government plans to continue using helicopters in search operations Sunday in Nepal to locate nine Koreans who have gone missing after a catastrophic flash flood devastated the Himalayan country, the foreign ministry said. Two helicopters are scheduled to be used: one chartered by the government's rapid response team and the other chartered by Doosan Enerbility. Flight authorization has yet to be granted, however, as ground conditions and decisions by Nepali authorities overseeing the rescue effort remain fluid. On Saturday, a government-charted helicopter carrying four rapid response team members flew twice from Kathmandu toward the flood site, becoming reportedly the only non-Nepali aircraft cleared to fly that day. The helicopter reportedly failed to land, and the search was instead conducted visually, with footage from the flight analyzed. Six employees of Doosan Enerbility and three of Korea South-East Power Co. remain missing since the massive floods struck Nepal's north-central Himalayan border area Wednesday. item.title: Icelanders reject EU-accession talks, broadcaster RUV reports
item.description: REYKJAVIK — Icelanders have voted to stay out of the European Union, broadcaster RUV reported on Sunday, rejecting a government push to reopen membership talks and siding with those who said Iceland's fishing waters were too important to risk. A "no" vote will disappoint Brussels, as some officials had cast Iceland as a low-risk case that could help ease scepticism toward EU enlargement and strategically strengthen the bloc when Arctic security is in focus. The government had framed its membership plan as a "now or never" moment, and Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir told voters in August that a "no" would put all EU speculation aside. "Yes" campaigners have said joining the bloc could ease high interest rates and offer more security in a world unsettled by war in Ukraine and U.S. President Donald Trump's rhetoric about annexing another Arctic island Greenland. "No" campaigners said EU membership would threaten the island's sovereignty and fishing waters. The referendum campaign has fuelled debate about Iceland's place in the world, Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir told reporters

item.title: Rescuers race to find thousands missing after Nepal-China glacier collapse
item.description: CHITWAN, Nepal/BEIJING — Rescuers in Nepal and China raced on Sunday to find thousands of people missing after a glacier collapse unleashed a catastrophic mudslide across the Himalayas, as they faced challenging weather conditions and rising water levels. Authorities said the death toll rose to 750 by Sunday morning, with more than 3,000 people missing on both sides of the Nepal-China border after a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris swept through mountain valleys and rivers on Wednesday, causing widespread devastation. The Red Cross has estimated that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Nepalese counterpart during a Saturday telephone call that the mudslide was their "most severe cross-border disaster" in recent years and that rescue operations had risen to an unprecedented level of difficulty and complexity, state broadcaster CCTV reported. item.title: Pony.ai to bring 200 Level 4 robotaxis to Korea by 2028
item.description: Chinese autonomous driving company Pony.ai is partnering with local mobility firm FutureLink to introduce 200 Level 4 self-driving taxis to Korea by 2028, as Chinese automakers and self-driving technology companies expand their presence in the domestic market. The two companies signed a strategic partnership on Friday in Seoul to introduce Pony.ai’s seventh-generation robotaxis to Korea, starting with 10 vehicles for domestic certification and adding 190 more after the certification process is completed. The companies plan to initially launch the robotaxi service in Seoul's autonomous driving pilot zone in Gangnam before gradually expanding it across the city, the wider Seoul metropolitan area and other major cities. The timing of the certification and commercial launch has not yet been finalized. FutureLink will handle regulatory certification, market entry, vehicle and service operations, data management, and localization, while Pony.ai will provide its seventh-generation autonomous driving vehicles and technology. The two companies are also considering establishing a joint venture i

item.title: Jeju tourism hit by safety concerns after mishandled missing person cases
item.description: Jeju's reputation as a safe travel destination is coming under strain after police prematurely closed a missing person case and several missing people were later found dead. With domestic visitor numbers falling, concerns are growing over safety on the island. According to the Jeju Tourism Association on Sunday, domestic visitor numbers fell year-on-year on all but one day between Aug. 19 and Aug. 29. Aug. 19 was also when the police’s premature closure of the missing person case began drawing widespread public attention. "I was planning to travel to Jeju with my family in early September, but we changed our destination to Gangwon Province because of the recent incidents," said Seo Ye-bin, a 26-year-old graduate student. "People are even sharing maps showing where missing-person cases have occurred. It just feels unsettling to visit Jeju right now." item.title: Korea's $20 bil. US investment unlikely to pressure won: BOK chief
item.description: Korea's planned annual investment of up to $20 billion in the United States is unlikely to put pressure on the won, as the local currency has become more resilient to external shocks, Bank of Korea (BOK) Gov. Shin Hyun-song said. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium in Wyoming on Friday (local time), Shin said the size of the investment was manageable, given Korea's foreign exchange reserves. "The memorandum of understanding says Korea will invest up to $20 billion annually in the U.S. While the investment could reach $20 billion, we could invest less, depending on the circumstances," Shin was quoted as saying in response to a question about whether the planned investment could put pressure on the won. item.title: Why president, chief justice are clashing over Supreme Court seat
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung and Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, at odds for more than a year, are now locked in their most direct confrontation yet over the appointment of a Supreme Court justice. Cheong Wa Dae said Friday it would not submit a confirmation motion to the National Assembly for Sohn Bong-ki, a senior judge at the Daegu District Court, and asked the chief justice to recommend another candidate. Senior presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said the powers to recommend and appoint justices are “assigned to different constitutional institutions,” arguing that Cho’s authority should respect the president’s substantive appointment power. The main opposition People Power Party (PPP) says that would undermine the chief justice’s constitutional authority and threaten judicial independence. But the dispute did not begin with Sohn’s nomination. Its roots go back to a Supreme Court ruling just weeks before the 2025 presidential election that threw Lee’s campaign into uncertainty. item.title: Iran's Khamenei urges Gulf rulers in written message to confront 'real enemy'
item.description: TEHRAN — Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei urged Muslim countries, particularly those in the Gulf, to unite against what he called their "real enemy" and said divisions among Muslims served the interests of their adversaries. The message was published on Khamenei's Telegram account for Islamic Unity Week, which marks the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad. It called for Muslim unity, cooperation in various fields and mutual defence, saying anyone who creates divisions among Muslims, "knowingly or unknowingly," helps Islam's enemies. It asked whether Palestinians would have been left "so helpless" if Muslims had been united. Khamenei has not been seen in public since being injured in U.S.-Israeli airstrikes six months ago that launched the Iran war, killing his father and previous supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. His call for unity echoes a statement he made on Friday to Iranians, when he said he had banned actions that harm social cohesion and urged authorities to avoid "discouraging statements" that weaken national and public morale. item.title: Household, self-employed debt raises alarm as BOK lifts key rate to 3%
item.description: The Bank of Korea's (BOK) recent decision to raise its policy rate to 3 percent is increasing concerns over the financial stability of already vulnerable borrowers, including the self-employed, analysts said Sunday. Delinquency rates have climbed to record highs, while total household debt has surpassed 2,000 trillion won ($1.45 trillion) for the first time. With a large share of these loans carrying variable rates, higher borrowing costs could put further strain on vulnerable borrowers and increase the risk of defaults. The central bank raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3 percent at Thursday's policy meeting, marking the second consecutive hike following its July increase. The impact is likely to be particularly burdensome for self-employed borrowers, as both outstanding debt and delinquent loans have reached record highs, while delinquency rates have climbed to alarming levels, raising concerns that the rate hike could further increase their interest burden and the risk of defaults. item.title: 1 dead, 5 wounded in Swiss shooting incident: police
item.description: GENEVA — A shooting in northern Switzerland has killed one person and injured at least five, some of them seriously, local police said on Sunday. Cantonal police in Aargau said a manhunt is underway and they appealed to the public for any film or pictures of the incident, which the mass-market Blick tabloid said had occurred at a rave party in the hippodrome. A video on its site recorded successive gunshots being fired. Large areas of the Aarau town are cordoned off, police said, and it has increased its presence beyond the town as a precaution. Switzerland has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in Europe although violent shootings are rare and it approved tighter gun control rules in 2019.

item.title: Why foreign tourists are trading palaces for peaks in Korea
item.description: Overseas visitors to Korea are increasingly choosing mountain peaks over historic palaces. On Sunday, the trend was highlighted when 11 members of France's Fédération Française de la Randonnée hiked in Bukhansan National Park with Culture Minister Chae Hwi-young and renowned climber Um Hong-gil. The visit is part of a larger group of about 40 association members currently touring Korea in three separate 11-day trips, hiking not just Mount Bukhan, but also Hahoe Folk Village in Andong, Mount Nam in Gyeongju, Mount Geumjeong in Busan, Suncheon Bay and a temple stay at Hwaeom Temple near Mount Jiri. The Korea Tourism Organization arranged the trip as part of its marketing push for Korean walking tourism. The timing lines up with a campaign the tourism agency launched in July with the Korea National Park Service, aiming to draw a combined 3 million visitors to national parks by 2028. item.title: SME biz sentiment up for 2nd month for Sept. but still below par
item.description: Korean smaller companies' business outlook rose for the second consecutive month for September but still remains below par, a poll showed Sunday. The survey of 3,060 small and midsized enterprises (SMEs) said the small business health index (SBHI) came to 84.8 for next month, up 4.8 points from August, according to the Korea Federation of SMEs. The index rose for two straight months since it reached 80 for August from 78.2. A reading below 100 indicates pessimists outnumber optimists. According to the findings, the SBHI for the manufacturing sector came to 87.1 for September, up 7 points from the prior month, with that for nonmanufacturing companies rising by 3.7 points to 83.7. More than 50 percent of the respondents cited sluggish sales as the biggest hurdle to their management, followed by rising raw material costs at 41 percent and cutthroat competition making up 31.4 percent. High labor costs was another factor causing concerns at 27.8 percent. item.title: Ticket scalping surges ahead of Seoul fireworks festival amid legal loophole
item.description: Ticket scalping is once again rampant ahead of the Seoul International Fireworks Festival, with tickets being resold at steep markups just a week before the annual event at Yeouido Hangang Park. The government has moved to tighten laws against ticket scalping, but fireworks festivals fall outside the scope of existing regulations, leaving authorities with no legal grounds to crack down on resales and allowing the problem to persist year after year. The festival, now in its 22nd year, is scheduled to take place Saturday. The annual event draws around 1 million spectators each year. Since 2024, Hanwha, the organizer of the festival, has been setting up designated viewing areas at Yeouido Hangang Park, offering seats through a lottery for spectators seeking a closer view of the fireworks. This year, Hanwha offers 700 paid seats at Nodeul Island, dubbed the Orange Play Zone, priced between 110,000 won ($79.70) and 220,000 won depending on the viewing area. item.title: Finance minister resumes G20 trip after brief cancellation amid Cabinet reshuffle
item.description: Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol, who was included in President Lee Jae Myung’s Cabinet shuffle on Sunday, departed for the United States to attend a meeting of Group of 20 finance ministers and central bank governors as originally planned after briefly canceling his trip, according to the ministry. “Koo departed as scheduled Sunday morning to attend the G20 gathering in Asheville, North Carolina, which runs Monday through Tuesday,” a ministry official said. Koo initially called off his U.S. trip after learning that he was set to be replaced in the Cabinet shuffle upon arriving at Incheon International Airport earlier in the day. Several hours later, the presidential office announced the Cabinet changes, with Lee nominating incumbent First Vice Minister Lee Hyoung-il as the new finance minister, among other appointments. Koo, however, reversed his decision and opted to make the trip as planned, given that he is expected to remain in office for about another month while his successor goes through a parliamentary confirmation hearing and formal appointment process. item.title: Nepal warns of more possible floods as communities grapple with devastation
item.description: DHADING, Nepal — Authorities in Nepal are warning of possible fresh flooding on Sunday and urged residents in flood-affected districts to remain on high alert after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River. Flood warning notices were sent to people's phones throughout Sunday morning, as rescue crews worked to clear a major highway connecting Kathmandu to one of the areas worst-hit by Wednesday's catasrophic floods. In the town of Galchhi, a group of residents sought higher ground on a nearby bridge and watched as the river roared by. People pointed to enormous rocks that had been washed downriver during the earlier floods, as others standing on a suspension bridge over the water were warned off with whistles. Along the river entire homes, vehicles and farm tractors could be seen jutting from the thick grey-brown sediment that has enveloped entire villages in the worst-hit flood areas. Rice terraces along riverside had experienced landslides, dropping parts of their field into the river. The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 750 dead and over 3,000 people missing after the lates

item.title: Hillstate Yangsan The Sky draws homebuyer interest as Yangsan market recovers
item.description: Hyundai E&C’s Hillstate Yangsan The Sky is drawing growing interest from homebuyers as apartment prices in Yangsan, South Gyeongsang Province, show early signs of recovery, while planned rail links are expected to improve connections to Busan and Ulsan. The development, located in the city’s Mulgeum area, comes to market at a time when newly built housing remains relatively limited in the area, a mature residential district with established schools, retail and public facilities, as well as access to Busan. Recent transactions in the area point to a gradual improvement in market conditions. An 84-square-meter unit in the neighborhood sold for 564 million won ($408,500) earlier this month, up about 81 million won from February, according to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. Transportation improvements are also expected to support the area’s appeal. The 11.43-kilometer Yangsan subway line is targeted to open in December, while a metropolitan rail line linking Ulsan, Yangsan and Busan is targeted for completion in 2031. item.title: Samsung Electronics, SK hynix's corporate tax tops $8.1 bil. in H1
item.description: Corporate taxes paid by Samsung Electronics Co. and SK hynix Inc. totaled a combined 11.2 trillion won ($8.1 billion) in the first half of this year amid the recent semiconductor supercycle, financial data showed Sunday. Samsung Electronics paid 3.99 trillion won in corporate taxes and SK hynix paid 7.22 trillion won in the first half, according to data from the Repository of Korea's Corporate Filings, operated by the Financial Supervisory Service. The two companies' combined corporate taxes jumped 167 percent from a year earlier, marking the second-highest first-half total on record. The figure followed the record 15.63 trillion won they paid in the first half of 2019, based on their record-high profits during a memory chip boom in 2018. Generally, companies pay corporate taxes in March for the previous fiscal year that ends in December and in August for their interim first-half profits. item.title: Over 350 police disciplinary actions overturned on appeal over 5 years
item.description: More than 350 disciplinary actions against police officers have been reduced, overturned or nullified over the past five years through appeals, data showed Sunday. The data, released by Rep. Park Sang-woong of the main opposition People Power Party based on figures received from the National Police Agency, showed such cases totaled 354 from 2021 to 2025. The figures raise concerns that police disciplinary actions carry little weight, given how often the outcomes are reversed through appeal proceedings. Meanwhile, the number of appeals filed rose to 411 last year, up 34.3 percent from 2021. In some cases, officers facing dismissal appealed and kept their jobs. In one such case, an officer dismissed over a drunk driving offense was reinstated after appeal. The importance of the disciplinary system has grown, experts say, as a recent string of high-profile misconduct and negligence cases have concerned the people, including a missing woman incident on Jeju Island in which a police officer quietly dropped the investigation and closed the case. item.description: Korea's monetary policy should focus on preventing core inflation from spreading broadly and remaining elevated as robust exports spill over into the broader economy and intensify demand-side inflationary pressures, a central bank report said Sunday. "As the recent strong performance in semiconductor exports spills over into domestic demand, there is a possibility that demand-side inflationary pressures will intensify in the future," said a report published by the Bank of Korea (BOK). The recent boom in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure has pushed up semiconductor prices and improved Korea's terms of trade, while the country has continued to benefit from robust semiconductor exports. In the first quarter, Korea's real gross domestic product (GDP) grew 3.8 percent from a year earlier, while real gross domestic income (GDI), which reflects changes in the terms of trade, expanded 13.2 percent. item.title: New jobs held by people in 20s, 30s decrease to record low in Q1
item.description: The number of new jobs held by people in their 20s and 30s fell to a record low in the first quarter, government data showed Sunday. A combined 2.36 million new jobs were held by people in their 20s and 30s in the January-March period, down 23,000 from a year earlier, according to data from the Korean Statistical Information Service, an online portal operated by the Ministry of Data and Statistics. The figure marked the lowest since the government began to compile such data in 2018. The number of new jobs held by people in their 20s fell by 26,000 to 1.34 million in the first quarter, also marking a record low. New jobs in manufacturing contracted by 24,000, accounting for the majority of the overall decline. For people in their 30s, the number of new jobs stood at 1.02 million, up 3,000 from a year earlier. Industry insiders attributed the decline in new jobs for younger people to the shrinking population of this age group, weaker hiring demand in manufacturing and companies' preference for experienced workers. item.title: Lee nominates 6 ministers in Cabinet reshuffle
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung reshuffled his Cabinet on Sunday, replacing ministers in six key posts as his administration faces mounting public criticism and falling approval ratings. Presidential chief of staff Kang Hoon-sik announced the nominations at a briefing at Cheong Wa Dae. Lee Hyoung-il, first vice minister of finance and economy, was tapped to serve as deputy prime minister for economic affairs and minister of finance and economy. Born in 1971, Lee is a veteran bureaucrat who has held key posts since joining the finance ministry in 1993, building expertise in both domestic and international economics as a senior economist at the World Bank and as commissioner of Statistics Korea. He has served as vice minister since June 2025. In a statement following his nomination, Lee said the Korean economy needs to take on new challenges to achieve a "great leap forward toward an irreplaceable Korea." He pledged to build on the momentum achieved over the past year while creating new investment and growth opportunities through three megaprojects, laying the groundwork for a rebound in potential

item.title: Seoul International Fireworks Festival 2026: Everything you need to know
item.description: This year's Seoul International Fireworks Festival is set for Saturday, with teams from Korea, the United States and Britain set to showcase fireworks displays unique to their respective countries. The festival, hosted by Hanwha Corp., is expected to attract over a million visitors, many of whom gather at Yeouido Hangang Park to enjoy the lightshow in its full glory. The collective anticipation is palpable, as Starbucks Yeouido Hangang Park seat packages offering panoramic views of the fireworks — priced up to 300,000 won ($220) — sold out in 30 seconds. Here are all the details you need. When is the festival happening? The fireworks festival will take place on Saturday from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m., with shows running from 8 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. Britain's Pyrotex Fireworx will kick off the show from 8 p.m. to 8:15 p.m., followed by the U.S.' Ace Pyro from 8:20 p.m. to 8:35 p.m. For the finale, Korea's Hanwha Corp.'s fireworks display will take place from 8:40 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. A five-minute break will take place between each performance. The fireworks festival will take place on Saturday from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m., with shows running from 8 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. Britain's Pyrotex Fireworx will kick off the show from 8 p.m. to 8:15 p.m., followed by the U.S.' Ace Pyro from 8:20 p.m. to 8:35 p.m. For the finale, Korea's Hanwha Corp.'s fireworks display will take place from 8:40 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. A five-minute break will take place between each performance. A pre-festival event is scheduled for Friday, from 1 p.m.

item.title: Venezuela's interim president says US energy deal will last 25 years
item.description: CARACAS — Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday that an energy agreement with the U.S. would remain in force for 25 years, target an increase in crude output to 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) and preserve the country's sovereignty over its natural resources. Rodriguez hailed the accord in a late-night address as a "historic" deal that would help revive the economy and boost government revenue, saying it would help shape the country's future. “This 25-year bilateral project envisages the development of 17 strategic oilfields with a production target of more than 1.5 million barrels per day," Rodriguez said on state broadcaster VTV. "That figure relates solely to the bilateral agreement between Venezuela and the United States." Rodriguez added that the agreement's target of 1.5 million bpd was only an initial goal and that the broader plan also included the development of eight greenfield oil blocks as part of a wider expansion of the country's energy sector. item.title: Traffic, crime, fine dust top Seoul residents' smart city concerns: poll
item.description: Seoul citizens named traffic congestion, nighttime crime and fine dust as the areas most in need of smart city solutions, a poll showed Sunday. The Korean megalopolis surveyed 8,531 Seoul residents online and offline from Feb. 10-21 last year as part of efforts to map out a smart city plan. Traffic, safety and the environment emerged as the three areas most in need of attention, cited by 37.5 percent, 21.2 percent and 16.2 percent of the respondents, respectively, according to the poll. When asked which areas most needed a smart city push specifically, the respondents again put traffic first at 30.1 percent, followed by safety at 27.5 percent and the environment at 18.8 percent. Within the traffic category, congestion was the top concern at 34.2 percent, followed by insufficient infrastructure at 18.5 percent and parking difficulties at 17 percent. item.title: Korean individual investors purchase net $7 bil. worth of US stocks in 2 months
item.description: Korean individual investors purchased over $7 billion worth of U.S. stocks over the past two months amid a correction in the local equity market, industry data showed Sunday. Retail investors bought a net $7.04 billion worth of stocks in the U.S. market from July 1 through Thursday, according to data from the online portal operated by the Korea Securities Depository. Over the same period, they purchased a net 8.75 trillion won ($6.34 billion) in the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) market and a net 1.57 trillion won in the secondary KOSDAQ market. In the United States, individuals bought a net $4.64 billion in July and $2.4 billion during the first 27 days of August. The two-month total was equivalent to 70 percent of their net purchases in the first half of the year, which totaled $9.87 billion. The shift came as the KOSPI underwent a correction after hitting a record closing high of 9,114.55 points on June 22. The index dropped to the 7,000-point level on the second trading day of July and has hovered in the 6,000-point range for more than a month since mid-July. Meanw

item.title: Russian strike on Ukrainian warehouse kills 37 in war's deadliest attack this year
item.description: MYLA, Ukraine — A Russian drone struck a warehouse west of Kyiv that Ukrainian officials say was storing shells, mines and other ammunition, sparking massive explosions and fires that swept through dozens of nearby homes and buildings and killing 37 people. The Friday night attack on the warehouse in Myla, a village in the Bucha district, was the war’s deadliest attack this year and came on the second of three days of nearly round-the-clock Russian strikes that have severely disrupted life in and around the Ukrainian capital. Attacks on the capital and, to a lesser extent, the rest of Ukraine have been nearly constant since Thursday. Kyiv officials say Russia builds up missile stocks and launches major attacks every few days, hoping to exhaust Ukrainian defenses through the sheer weight of numbers. The warehouse strike sparked fires that raced through homes and damaged at least 50 residential buildings, said Tymur Tkachenko, who heads the local regional military administration. He was later cited by local media as saying 34 of the people killed were residents of a care home for elde

item.title: N. Korea names new defense minister amid modernization drive
item.description: North Korea has replaced its defense minister in a reshuffle of senior military leadership, state media reported Sunday, as the country accelerates its military modernization push and tightens discipline within the ranks. Kim Song-gi, director of the General Political Bureau of the North's Korean People's Army, was appointed as the country's new defense minister, replacing No Kwang-chol, according to the North's Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). No was removed as defense minister and from the party's central leadership and appointed first vice-director of the Munitions Industry Department of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea (WPK). The reshuffle was decided at the second meeting of the ninth WPK Central Military Commission held the previous day, which was guided by leader Kim Jong-un, the report said. In the latest reshuffle, veteran military official Pak Jong-chon was appointed vice-chairman of the WPK Central Military Commission after being re-elected as a member of the party's Central Committee and Politburo. Pak returned to the forefront of the North's military leadership after step

item.title: Fake office in Seoul helps reclusive youth fight social isolation
item.description: In a quiet community center in western Seoul, 33 young adults recently committed to a novel daily routine: waking up, dressing and reporting for work at a company that exists entirely to help them reenter society. For many, stepping through the front door marked their tentative first foray into the outside world after months or even years spent largely behind closed bedroom doors. They are the newest employees at "NEET Company," a virtual firm operating in Seodaemun District through Oct. 19. Despite its corporate veneer, this office imposes no sales targets, demands no career milestones and measures no corporate performance metrics. Designed specifically for reclusive youth and those classified as NEET — an acronym for adults not in education, employment or training — the municipal initiative acts as a low-stakes buffer zone. Its goal is to help participants rebuild daily life rhythms and human connections without the overwhelming pressure of traditional competitive employment. The program addresses a silent epidemic sweeping Korea. According to comprehensive national health and welfa

item.title: As women crowd ballparks, K-drama actors take on new professions
item.description: Kim Woo-bin and Ryu Seung-ryong have little in common in terms of age or acting style. Their filmographies, however, are about to gain one common thread, and it has something to do with baseball. In December, Kim is set to appear in tvN drama “Gift,” a tentative English title, as a former baseball player who coaches a high school baseball team. Ryu, meanwhile, stars as a famous baseball player in the film “Portrait of a Family,” which opens next month. They are not the only ones. Suddenly baseball players and coaches have become some of the most sought-after characters in the Korean drama and film industry; Gong Myoung is currently filming MBC drama “Your Ground,” a tentative English title set to air at the end of this year, in which he plays a pitcher.
